gaps.sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
gaps.explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
gaps.hint: snap at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
gaps.explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

gaps.sentence: 'We'll be arriving on the red-eye,' they said. They said they ___ on the red-eye.
gaps.explanation: 'Will be arriving' backshifts to 'would be arriving'.

gaps.sentence: 'When does the library open?' she asked. She asked ___ the library opened.
gaps.explanation: The original question word 'when' is kept in the reported clause.
